comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-taught programme has two prescribed 60 EC years. The final year includes a 30 EC autumn choice, 18 EC of compulsory spring coursework and a 12 EC thesis. The regulations list four ways to fill the choice semester.
components: Tilburg also recommends uncredited GROW activities throughout the degree.
Builds on Introduction to Data Analysis and extends statistical modelling in R.

Choose 30 EC of exchange, a 24 EC internship plus a 6 EC elective, two 15 EC school minors, or a 30 EC Tilburg University minor. The internship requires at least 90 EC and compliance with its handbook.
The regulations require at least 120 EC for the sixth-semester thesis, or 138 EC from semester seven onward. The thesis syllabus gives further entry and participation requirements.

core: Organisation, strategy, leadership and human-resource management
Accounting, finance, investment and economics for business
Marketing, entrepreneurship and applied business decisions
Operations, supply chains and process improvement
Data analysis, programming and management information systems
Business research, law, ethics, sustainability and thesis work
adjacent: Business analytics, digital systems and operational decision-making
questions: How do organisations make strategic, financial, marketing and people decisions?
How can data, digital systems and process analysis improve business performance?
How can firms combine entrepreneurship and performance with sustainability and ethics?

alternatives.label: Business management, strategy & finance
alternatives.concept: Study how businesses make decisions about finances, markets, people and strategy. Combine accounting and economics with marketing research, negotiation and organisational leadership.
alternatives.labelReason: Accounting, finance, marketing and research support strategy, negotiation and organisational leadership.
progression: Business and economics foundations lead into accounting, international economics, marketing and business law. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics and advanced organisational study.

alternatives.label: Business analytics & digital systems
alternatives.concept: Use data, software and models to investigate business decisions. Study databases, econometrics, machine learning and optimisation alongside strategy and organisational change.
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, statistics, econometrics, databases and optimisation support the study of business decisions and processes.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the management option, this schedule gives more depth to programming, data handling, prediction and optimisation. It provides general tools for analysing business processes.
progression: Programming and mathematics precede algorithms and optimisation. Data Science precedes Machine Learning and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics prepares for Econometrics.

alternatives.label: Responsible entrepreneurship & sustainable organisations
alternatives.concept: Develop business ideas and assess their environmental and social effects. Combine entrepreneurship and strategy with product life-cycle analysis, resource recovery and sustainability governance.
alternatives.labelReason: Entrepreneurship, strategy, ethics and governance connect to evidence on the environmental impacts of products and organisations.
alternatives.distinctness: Life-cycle analysis, resource recovery, sustainable farming and energy design provide an applied environmental focus. Ethics and public economics help evaluate choices about innovation and governance.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which prepares for resource recovery and renewable-system design. Business foundations precede business law and digital strategy.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

Evaluates how AI changes firms, markets and economic decisions, with attention to its limits.
Uses comparative law to analyse cross-border business transactions and resolve legal problems.
Studies financial instruments, valuation, markets and financial institutions.
Uses basic microeconomics and macroeconomics to explain markets, consumer behaviour and aggregate activity.
Uses international macroeconomic models to analyse trade, financial conditions and policy.
Analyses consumer choice, imperfect competition and economic allocation.
Evaluates public policy and market failures through efficiency, equity and externalities.
Uses statistical estimators and model diagnostics to analyse causal questions and prediction.
Uses product research and iterative design to develop and evaluate consumer product ideas.
Uses customer research and consumer psychology to plan engagement and evaluate communication and customer experience.
Develops and evaluates plans for organisations to adopt and manage digital change.
Designs and carries out market research, analysing and presenting findings on customer preferences.
Examines how trade, institutions and political and cultural conditions shape firms’ international decisions.
Uses design thinking to identify user needs and develop a venture concept and prototype.
Develops empirical research design, measurement, sampling and statistical analysis in a student project.
Develops personal leadership and applies emotional intelligence, prioritisation and self-reflection.
Examines leadership styles and applies rhetoric and persuasion to organisational communication.
Studies emotion regulation, psychological safety and leadership under pressure.
Studies how motivation, leadership, conflict, culture and organisational structure affect change.
Uses structured negotiation, interest analysis and framing to evaluate strategies and agreements.
Uses ethics and psychology to examine AI, including privacy, fairness, responsibility and human interaction.
Uses search and optimisation to design decision-making algorithms.
Models and queries structured data using relational design and SQL.
Develops and analyses algorithms and data structures for efficient computing.
Cleans, joins, analyses and visualises tabular, textual and spatial data in R.
Develops and evaluates regression, classification and other predictive learning models.
Builds and evaluates neural networks for images, text and time-series tasks.
Uses Python to develop, test and debug programs.
Uses calculus, optimisation and differential equations for modelling.
Uses matrices, transformations, eigenvalues and least squares to represent quantitative problems.
Develops probability and statistical inference, including estimation and uncertainty.
Uses resource recovery and recycling cases to evaluate material circularity and environmental trade-offs.
Studies how institutions, markets and communities govern environmental choices and trade-offs.
Evaluates how farming practices and innovations affect food systems, biodiversity and resources.
Introduces planetary boundaries, modelling and basic environmental science for sustainability questions.
Relates physical, chemical and material properties to environmental performance and sustainability.
Studies climate change, impacts, adaptation and mitigation in social and ecological settings.
Assesses the environmental, social and economic effects of products and services across their life cycles.
Evaluates energy consumption and renewable options through technical and economic analysis for a partner organisation.
Uses competing theories and philosophical argument to evaluate ethical questions.
Develops ethically grounded qualitative research design, data collection, analysis and communication.
Analyses argument, rhetorical form and delivery, with practice in persuasive communication.

candidates.label: Business analytics, digital systems and operations

selection.assessment: The broad management option covers business functions and organisational decisions. Separate options emphasise quantitative and digital business methods or responsible enterprise and sustainability. Quantitative methods support operations questions without forming a supply-chain specialisation.

notes.text: Tilburg requires courses in operations and supply-chain management, human resources and applied business practice, followed by a 12 EC business thesis. UCR offers related combinations of business, analytics and sustainability, with independent research as an option.

blocks: Both introduce financial reporting and accounting analysis. UCR also introduces management accounting and investment appraisal.
Both study marketing decisions and customer needs. UCR emphasises engagement and brand strategy.
Both analyse and plan organisational strategy. UCR focuses on digital transformation.
Both study legal frameworks for businesses. Tilburg focuses on Dutch company law and UCR on cross-border transactions.
Both examine how people, teams and institutions shape organisational behaviour. UCR adds an emphasis on leadership.
Both analyse investments and financial markets. UCR also studies banking and financial institutions.
Both use calculus and optimisation. UCR applies mathematical tools in a broader scientific setting.
Both use R to work with data. Tilburg includes spreadsheet methods and business applications.
Both introduce microeconomic and macroeconomic ideas. Tilburg applies them to business decisions.
Both study aspects of organising information. UCR focuses on database design and queries.
Both use regression and statistical inference. UCR develops econometric methods for causal and predictive questions.
Both develop ethical reasoning. Tilburg applies it specifically to organisations and business decisions.
Both evaluate how organisations create value while managing environmental effects. UCR focuses on product and service life cycles.
Both develop research design and empirical reasoning. Tilburg applies these methods to business management.

audience.programmeDescription: Business Administration at Tilburg University studies how organisations make decisions about strategy, finance, marketing and operations. Students apply these ideas to business cases and complete a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in management and finance, business analytics and digital systems, or entrepreneurship and sustainability. Tilburg includes a dedicated sequence in operations and supply chains, business practice and a required thesis.
